question: Can native evolution improve the temporary neutral-to-quantum conversion schedule against matched reconstructed MPSO 5+0 and 5+1?
scenario: 5 dimensions, 10 peaks, severity 1, period 5000, correlation 0, nexcess 1, 500000 counted objective queries
selection: Minimum development mean offline error among complete valid native programs, including the seed; ties by earlier generation, then source SHA256.
fresh_comparison_condition: A source-distinct selected descendant has a strictly lower development mean error than the seed and is not established execution-equivalent to it.
fresh_freeze_order: Freeze exact selected and reference sources and this analysis before generating eight fresh environment/optimizer seed pairs.
effect_direction: Negative selected-minus-reference offline error favors the selected schedule.
case_weighting: Equal weight for each of the eight independent paired cases in this single scenario.

bootstrap.resampling_unit: Independent environment/optimizer case pair, preserving all paired method outcomes together.
bootstrap.interval: Descriptive 95% percentile bootstrap interval of the paired mean; numpy default_rng; no particle/update-level resampling.

influence: Retain every case. Report largest absolute case contribution, fraction of net mean where defined, and largest absolute completed-environment contribution; no outlier removal.
behavior: Equal-case summaries of temporary neutral count distributions, fraction of neutral updates converted, conversion by observed time since detected change, and measured ordinary/temporary/permanent quantum contributions to shared-best improvement.
recovery: Use saved actual query offsets after environmental boundaries. Exclude initial environment; average environments within a case, then give cases equal weight. Never interpolate unrecorded immediate error.
examples: Use prospectively recorded first update, first detected-change update, and first updates reaching one-quarter, one-half and three-quarters of the query budget in each case; additionally show the most favorable and unfavorable completed-environment contrasts as explicitly post hoc examples.
development_interpretation: All development comparisons are selected-data descriptions; intervals do not correct selection bias and are not a gate for continuing native search.
fresh_interpretation: Eight fresh pairs provide exploratory evidence in one chapter-aligned setting. They do not replicate Table 3's 50-run experiment, establish superiority over all chapter algorithm families, or identify a benefit of Shinka as a search method or of any engine feature.
